summary: Hand-traced the fitter over the new test inputs (width=320, available_height=50, dense=True, 1 H-statement + 4 P301+P310+P330, all texts 8 chars). The decisive rejection now happens in the horizontal_fit guard, not the height check: at font 6.4 pt / 2 precaution columns the block height is exactly 50.0 (= available_height, so the height condition passes) while horizontal_fit is False, and the fitter falls through to the 6.0 pt / 2-column candidate (height 49.2, horizontal_fit True), which is what the test asserts. Prior medium finding is closed. No critical/high/medium defect in the delta; one low brittleness note.

findings.defect: The test only asserts the final outcome (font_size == 6.0, block_height <= 50); it never asserts that the rejected 6.4 pt candidate actually fit vertically. The two margins that make it a horizontal-guard test are razor-thin: at 6.4 pt / 2 precaution columns block_height is exactly 50.0 against available_height 50 (app/label_stub.py:1112,1132) and the first-line width is 86.016 pt against a 85.333 pt limit (app/label_stub.py:1097-1103), a 0.68 pt margin. Any future change to padding (34), the dense line_height ladder (7.0/6.6), or the 0.56 glyph-width factor can silently push the 6.4 pt candidate over 50 pt in height, at which point the test still passes but once again proves nothing about horizontal_fit — the exact regression the prior review flagged.
findings.reasoning: A guard regression test that can degrade into a pass-for-the-wrong-reason without failing gives false confidence about column-overlap protection. Minimal fix: assert the intermediate state directly, e.g. compute the 6.4 pt / 2-column candidate (or temporarily relax the horizontal guard) and assert its block_height <= 50, so the test fails loudly if the vertical path becomes the rejecting condition.
